title: Fix: make Qwen3.5-0.8B better at math
summary:
Claude Opus 5.5 got Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights in a Python sandbox, a budget of 10, 25 or 50 forward passes (64 GSM8K/MATH training problems each, original vs edited weights side by side), and the task "make this model better at math by editing its weights, without training or gradients". Sampling followed the original (thinking, temperature 0.6, 32,768 tokens); final edits were scored on MATH-500 (4 samples), GSM8K and IFEval (2 samples each). The unedited model reproduces the original's baseline: MATH-500 6.7% (original 7.9%), 93% of answers running to the token limit.

Every run found the same failure (endless "Wait, …" loops) and fixed it: MATH-500 rose to 51.4% / 55.2% / 58.1% with 10 / 25 / 50 forward passes (+44.6 / +48.5 / +51.4 points, 95% CIs all above +41), GSM8K to 64.8–68.2%, IFEval to 43.6–54.2%, and the share hitting 32k fell from 93% to 29–39%. By the pre-registered rule the 50-pass result replicates the original (48.1% MATH-500, 67.1% GSM8K, 62.3% IFEval, 33% at the limit). Unlike the original, 10 passes were already enough.

Claude's edits differ from the original's. Instead of removing a direction from the layer-15/19 MLPs (131,072 weights), every run scaled the final RMSNorm (all logits ×0.6–0.68, i.e. a higher effective temperature) and made "Wait" less and `</think>` more likely, through the tied embedding rows (b25: 8,192 weights; b50: 6,144) or, at 10 passes, the outputs of layers 20–23. A pre-registered control isolates the temperature part: the final-norm scaling alone lifts MATH-500 only to 20.9–22.1% (looping turns into rambling: 77–79% still hit the limit); the token-level changes add 29–37 points more, so all three edits "do more than change temperature" by the pre-registered rule. On Gemma 3 270M, which barely loops, Claude's best edit (a pure temperature change) moved MATH-500 by −0.8 points [−1.9, +0.2] (9.2% → 8.3%), as in the original. All edits were verified (every other tensor bit-identical); no run broke the no-forward-pass rule. API cost $8.48 for Exp 8.

runs.label: Qwen3.5-0.8B · 10 forward passes (×64 problems)
runs.answer: Final norm ×0.6, so logits are 0.6× and T=0.6 acts like T≈1.0 (presence penalty ≈2.5). Layers 20–23 attention/MLP outputs: removed 35% of the "Wait"-readout direction; layer 23 MLP: amplified the `</think>`-readout component by 1.3×. This stops the loops and the endless second-guessing.

runs.label: Qwen3.5-0.8B · 25 forward passes (×64 problems)
runs.answer: Final norm (1+w) scaled ×0.6 (logits ×0.6, i.e. temperature 0.6→~1.0, which breaks the loops); tied embedding rows scaled: Wait/ Wait/ wait/wait ×0.8, Hmm/ Hmm ×0.9 (less "Wait" rambling), </think> ×1.3 (ends thinking sooner). Practice accuracy went from ~6–10% to ~60%.
runs.reasoning_excerpt:
I raised practice accuracy from about 6–10% to about 60% by changing 8,192 weights in two tensors. The final saved edit is exactly the version tested in the last run, on 256 new problems: accuracy went from 10.2% to 60.5% (paired gain +50.4 ± 3.1 points). GSM8K went from 9% to 63% and MATH from 11% to 58%.

The original model's problem wasn't really weak math. About 94% of its answers ran to the 32,768-token limit, almost all stuck repeating the same "Wait, …" lines, so it never reached `</think>` or a boxed answer. Whenever it did finish, it was right every time.

runs.label: Qwen3.5-0.8B · 50 forward passes (×64 problems)
runs.answer: Final norm weights scaled so (1+w) is 0.68× the original, which multiplies all logits by 0.68 (sampling temp 0.6 acts like ~0.88). The 4 "Wait"/"wait" embedding rows are scaled ×0.7 and the `</think>` row ×1.25. This breaks the endless repetition loops and cuts self-doubt so more answers finish.

runs.label: Gemma 3 270M-it · 25 forward passes (×64 problems)
runs.answer: Final norm gain (1+w) scaled by 0.86, so all logits are ×0.86, like sampling at temperature ≈1.16. Lower temperature clearly hurt. This roughly halves answers that loop to the 8,192-token limit, but its accuracy gain over the original is about zero, within noise.
runs.reasoning_excerpt:
EDIT: Final norm gain (1+w) scaled by 0.86, so all logits are ×0.86, like sampling at temperature ≈1.16. Lower temperature clearly hurt. This roughly halves answers that loop to the 8,192-token limit, but its accuracy gain over the original is about zero, within noise.

I didn't find an edit that clearly makes the model better at math. The saved edit has a reliable side effect (less looping), but its accuracy effect is too small to tell from noise.

**How the edit works:** the model has no final logit softcapping, and the output layer reads the final RMSNorm output. Multiplying the norm's gain (1+w) by α therefore multiplies every logit by α, which is the same as sampling at temperature 1/α. It's a 640-weight change and nothing was lost to bf16 rounding.
